title: 490. Sets, Logic, Reasoning & Proof: Conditional Statements
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: State the one case in which a conditional statement is false.
questions.question: When is the conditional statement \(p\implies q\) false?

options.label: A
options.text: Only when \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false

questions.explanation: The conditional "if \(p\), then \(q\)" makes a promise only for the case in which \(p\) holds. It is broken, and therefore false, only when \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false. When \(p\) is false the promise is not tested, and the conditional counts as true.
questions.hint: Think of the conditional as a promise that can be broken in only one way.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a conditional whose hypothesis is false.
questions.question: Let \(p\) be false and \(q\) be true. What is the truth value of \(p\implies q\)?
questions.explanation: A conditional is false only when its hypothesis is true and its conclusion is false. Here the hypothesis \(p\) is false, so the conditional is true regardless of \(q\).
questions.hint: Check whether this is the single case that makes a conditional false.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the hypothesis of a conditional statement.
questions.question: In the statement "If an integer is divisible by \(4\), then it is even", what is the hypothesis?
questions.explanation: In "if \(p\), then \(q\)", the part \(p\) following "if" is the hypothesis and the part \(q\) following "then" is the conclusion. Here the hypothesis is that the integer is divisible by \(4\); being even is the conclusion.
questions.hint: The hypothesis is the condition introduced by the word "if".

questions.concept: A conditional with a false arithmetic hypothesis
questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of a conditional whose hypothesis is a false arithmetic statement.
questions.question: What is the truth value of the statement "If \(2+2=5\), then \(3\) is even"?
questions.explanation: The hypothesis "\(2+2=5\)" is false. A conditional with a false hypothesis is true, whatever its conclusion; such a statement is called vacuously true. The falsity of the conclusion "\(3\) is even" does not matter here.
questions.hint: Determine the truth value of the hypothesis first.

questions.concept: A conditional with a true hypothesis and false conclusion
questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of a conditional in its one false case.
questions.question: What is the truth value of the statement "If \(3\) is odd, then \(4\) is odd"?
questions.explanation: The hypothesis "\(3\) is odd" is true, and the conclusion "\(4\) is odd" is false. This is exactly the case in which a conditional is false.
questions.hint: Find the truth values of the hypothesis and the conclusion separately.

questions.learningObjective: Express a conditional using negation and disjunction.
questions.question: Which compound proposition is logically equivalent to \(p\implies q\)?
questions.explanation:
The conditional is false only when \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false. The disjunction \(
eg p\lor q\) is false only when \(
eg p\) is false and \(q\) is false, which is the same case. So the two are equivalent. The expression \(p\lor
eg q\) is false when \(p\) is false and \(q\) is true, a different row.
questions.hint: Find the single row in which each expression is false and compare.

questions.concept: Truth table column of a conditional
questions.learningObjective: Write the truth table column of a conditional.
questions.question: The rows of a truth table are ordered by \((p,q)\) as \((T,T)\), \((T,F)\), \((F,T)\), \((F,F)\). What is the column for \(p\implies q\)?
questions.explanation: The conditional is false only in the row \((T,F)\). In the two rows with \(p\) false it is true. So the column is \(T,F,T,T\). The column \(T,F,F,T\) belongs to the biconditional, which also requires the converse.
questions.hint: Only one row makes a conditional false.

questions.learningObjective: Write the negation of a conditional statement.
questions.question: Which proposition is logically equivalent to \(\neg(p\implies q)\)?
questions.explanation: The conditional is false exactly when \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false, so its negation is true exactly then: \(p\land\neg q\). The negation of a conditional is a conjunction, not another conditional; \(p\implies\neg q\) is true whenever \(p\) is false, so it is a different statement.
questions.hint: Describe the one situation in which the conditional fails.

questions.learningObjective: Translate a sentence with "only if" into a conditional.
questions.question: Which conditional expresses the sentence "\(p\) only if \(q\)"?
questions.explanation: "\(p\) only if \(q\)" says that \(p\) cannot hold without \(q\): whenever \(p\) is true, \(q\) must be true. That is \(p\implies q\). The sentence "\(p\) if \(q\)" would be \(q\implies p\). For example, "an integer is divisible by \(4\) only if it is even" means "if it is divisible by \(4\), then it is even".
questions.hint: Ask what must be true whenever \(p\) is true.

questions.learningObjective: Find a value that makes an open conditional false.
questions.question: For which positive integer \(n\) is the statement "If \(n\) is prime, then \(n\) is odd" false?
questions.explanation: The conditional is false only when the hypothesis is true and the conclusion is false: \(n\) must be prime and not odd. The number \(2\) is prime and even, so it makes the statement false. For \(n=9\) the hypothesis is false, because \(9\) is not prime, so the conditional is true for that value.
questions.hint: Look for a value that satisfies the hypothesis but violates the conclusion.
